questions.question: Which two numbers need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 119 + 11 × 5 – 153 ÷ 17 = 201
questions.questionHtml:
Which two numbers need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

119 + 11 × 5 – 153 ÷ 17 = 201
questions.solution:
BODMAS rule:

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) 17 and 5. So the equation will become:

⇒ 119 + 11 × 17 - 153 ÷ 5 = 201

⇒ 119 + 11 × 17 - 30.6 = 201

⇒ 119 + 187 - 30.6 = 201

⇒ 306 - 30.6 = 201

⇒ 275.4 ≠ 201

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) 119 and 17. So the equation will become:

⇒ 17 + 11 × 5 - 153 ÷ 119 = 201

⇒ 17 + 11 × 5 - 1.2857 = 201

⇒ 17 + 55 - 1.2857 = 201 

⇒ 72 - 1.2857 = 201

⇒ 70.7143 ≠ 201

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) 119 and 153. So the equation will become:

⇒ 153 + 11 x 5 - 119 ÷ 17 = 201

⇒ 153 + 11 x 5 - 7 = 201

⇒ 153 + 55 - 7 = 201

⇒ 208 - 7 = 201

⇒ 201 = 201

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) 11 and 17. So the equation will become:

⇒ 119 + 17 × 5 - 153 ÷ 11 = 201

⇒ 119 + 17 × 5 - 13.90 = 201

⇒ 119 + 85 - 13.90 = 201

⇒ 204 - 13.90 = 201

⇒ 190.1 ≠ 201

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "119 and 153".

questions.solution:
Eight person: Bindu, Krunal, Manoj, Nilima, Omkar, Piyush, Renu and Sundar are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) Sundar sits second to the right of Piyush.

2) Only two persons sit between Sundar and Krunal.

 

3) Omkar sits opposite to Bindu, who is not an immediate neighbour of Krunal and Piyush.

4) Manoj sits third to the right of Bindu.

5)  Nilima is the immediate neighbour of Krunal and Bindu.

6) Only one position left for Renu.

Clearly, Nilima sits opposite the one who sits to the immediate left of Renu. 

Hence, the correct answer is "Nilima sits opposite the one who sits to the immediate left of Renu".

questions.question: Which two digits should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 37 + 1152 × 8 ÷ 768 − 47 = 22
questions.questionHtml:
Which two digits should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

37 + 1152 × 8 ÷ 768 − 47 = 22
questions.solution:
BODMAS rule:

Option 1) 5 and 6

After interchanging the digits we get: 

⇒ 37 + 1162 × 8 ÷ 758 - 47 = 22

⇒ 37 + 1162 × 0.010 - 47 = 22

⇒ 37 + 12.26 - 47 = 22

⇒ 49.26 - 47 = 22

⇒ 2.26 ≠ 22

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) 4 and 5

After interchanging the digits we get: 

⇒ 37 + 1142 × 8 ÷ 768 - 57 = 22

⇒ 37 + 1142 × 0.010 - 57 = 22

⇒ 37 + 11.42 - 57 = 22

⇒ 48.42 - 57 = 22

⇒ -8.58 ≠ 22

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) 3 and 4

After interchanging the digits we get:

⇒ 47 + 1152 × 8 ÷ 768 - 37 = 22

⇒ 47 + 1152 × \(\frac{8}{768}\) - 37 = 22

⇒ 47 + 3 × \(\frac{8}{2}\) - 37 = 22

⇒ 47 + 12 - 37 = 22

⇒ 59 - 37 = 22

⇒ 22 = 22

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) 2 and 3

After interchanging the digits we get:

⇒ 27 + 1152 × 8 ÷ 768 − 47 = 22

⇒ 27 + 1152 × 0.010 - 47 = 22

⇒ 27 + 11.52 - 47 = 22

⇒ 38.52 - 47 = 22 

⇒ - 8.48 ≠ 22

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "3 and 4".

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of plant disease?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a type of plant disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Blight.

Key Points

  • Blight refers to a type of plant disease caused by fungal or bacterial pathogens.
  • These pathogens cause cell death or necrosis, and when large areas of plants have been quickly killed, the disease is described as blight.
  • There are different types of blight that can affect your plants and understanding how to best treat them is crucial for their health.
  • Early blight, also known as target spot, is a common disease of tomatoes and potatoes.
  • The fungus can infect the leaves, stems and fruit of tomatoes and may explain why your tomatoes are dying.

Additional Information

Diseases Features 
Mastitis 
  • Mastitis is an infection that develops in breast tissue.
  • The painful condition causes one breast to become swollen, red and inflamed.
  • Breastfeeding women are most likely to get mastitis, although it can affect men and women who aren’t nursing.
Botulism
  • Botulism (or botulism poisoning) is a rare but very serious illness that transmits through food, contact with contaminated soil, or through an open wound.
  • Botulism poisoning is due to a toxin produced by a type of bacteria called Clostridium botulinum.
  • Although very common, these bacteria can only thrive in conditions where there’s no oxygen.
  • Certain food sources, such as home-canned foods, provide a potent breeding ground.
Coccidiosis
  • Coccidiosis is any of several gastrointestinal infections of humans and other animals produced by sporozoan parasites known as coccidia (subclass Coccidia).
  • Coccidiosis in animals occurs most commonly in cats, birds, dogs, rabbits, poultry, cattle and other livestock, and rodent.
  • Coccidiosis may be controlled by sanitary conditions and possibly by the administration of certain sulfonamides, arsenicals, and antibiotics.

questions.question: Which of the following events occurred before 1919?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following events occurred before 1919?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Partition of Bengal.

Key Points 

  • Partition of Bengal 
    • Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on 20th July 1905.
    • The partition came into effect on 16th October 1905.
    • At that time of partition, Bengal was the biggest province of British India that included Bihar and parts of Orissa.
    • The British argued that the division was for administrative convenience.
    • The partition of the Bengal is an example of the British policy of divide and rule.
    • The main reason for the partition of Bengal was to destroy the political influence of the educated middle class among whom the Bengali intelligentsia was the most prominent.
    • The swadeshi movement started to protest against the partition of Bengal.

questions.question: As per the theory of demographic transition, the post-transitional stage of demographic transition is characterised by ______.
questions.questionHtml: As per the theory of demographic transition, the post-transitional stage of demographic transition is characterised by ______.

options.text: high and nearly equal birth and death rates
options.html: high and nearly equal birth and death rates

options.text: falling birth rates and high death rates
options.html: falling birth rates and high death rates

options.text: falling death rates and high birth rates
options.html: falling death rates and high birth rates

options.text: low and nearly equal birth and death rates
options.html: low and nearly equal birth and death rates

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: 'low and nearly equal birth and death rates'.

Key Points

  • The post-transitional stage of demographic transition is characterised by low and nearly equal birth and death rates.
    • This statement is correct.
    • The post-transition stage marks the stabilization of population growth. Both birth rates and death rates are low and relatively equal. This results in negligible or even negative population growth.
    • Examples of such societies include Japan and Germany, where birth rates are well below replacement levels, and population decline is observed.
  • High and nearly equal birth and death rates
    • This statement is incorrect.
    • High birth and death rates typically describe the pre-transition stage of demographic transition, not the post-transitional stage.
    • In the pre-transition stage, both rates are high, leading to low net population growth. As societies move forward in the transition, these rates fall and eventually stabilize at lower levels.
  • Falling birth rates and high death rates
    • This statement is incorrect.
    • Falling birth rates and high death rates are characteristics of the early transition stage.
    • As death rates begin to fall due to improvements in healthcare and living conditions, birth rates typically remain high for some time before beginning to decline.
  • Falling death rates and high birth rates
    • This statement is incorrect.
    • Falling death rates and high birth rates characterize the early transition stage, where population growth accelerates due to improved healthcare and nutrition, but birth rates remain high due to cultural and social factors.

Additional Information

  • Demographic Transition Stages:
    • Stage 1: Pre-transition - Both birth rates and death rates are high, leading to low population growth.
    • Stage 2: Early transition - Death rates fall due to improvements in healthcare, while birth rates remain high, causing rapid population growth.
    • Stage 3: Late transition - Birth rates start to decline, and population growth begins to slow down.
    • Stage 4: Post-transition - Both birth rates and death rates are low, leading to stable or shrinking population size.

questions.questionHtml: In a ΔABC, D, E and F are the mid-points of side BC, CA and AB respectively. If BC = 14.4 cm, CA = 15.2 cm and AB = 12.4 cm, what is the perimeter (in cm) of the ΔDEF?

Given:

BC = 14.4 cm

CA = 15.2 cm

AB = 12.4 cm

Concept used:

Midpoint theorem - The line segment in a triangle joining the midpoint of two sides of the triangle is said to be parallel to its third side and is also half of the length of the third side.

Calculation:

F and E are the mid point of AB and AC

So, according to the concept,

FE = (BC/2)

Similarly,

DE = (AB/2) and FD = (AC/2)

Now,

Perimeter of ΔDEF = DE + FE + FD

⇒ (BC/2) + (AB/2) + (AC/2)

⇒ 1/2(BC + AB + AC)

⇒ 1/2(14.4 + 12.4 + 15.2)

⇒ 1/2(42)

⇒ 21

∴ The perimeter (in cm) of the ΔDEF is 21.

questions.solution:
Total of three numbers = 112 × 3 ⇒ 336. Let 2nd number be 3a, 1st number × 1/3 = 3a ⇒ 1st number = 3a × 3 = 9a

Alternate segment theorem = The angle between a tangent and a chord is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

Diameter makes an angle of 90 degree on circumference

Calculation:

According to the concept,

So, ∠BCA = 180° - 42° - 90° 

⇒ 48°

Now, according to the concept,

∠MAB = ∠BCA

So, ∠MAB = 48°

∴ The measure of ∠MAB is 48°.
